beats.beat: Functional additives are chemicals added to a material to change how it behaves; chemically modified minerals are minerals treated to do a specific job. Those two families, plus soft and hard minerals, are the product range the filing describes.

The filing argues the portfolio is spread across products and across user industries — two of six strengths it lists, the others being import substitution, support of the holding company, product innovation and R&D, and the management team.

The route to market is not the company's own. It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell through that network, and states it derives substantial synergies from that promoter — the filing also refers to it as the holding company.
Customer concentration is high and barely moves: the top ten customers were about 59%, 57% and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017 respectively.
Exports over the past five years totalled ₹1,068.18 lakh across three countries — Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka — so the business is overwhelmingly domestic.
None of the customer base is locked in. The company has no long-term or definitive agreements with customers and relies on purchase orders to govern volume, pricing and other terms.

beats.beat: The restated statements cover six periods: the years ended March 2013 through March 2017, and the six months ended September 30, 2017.

Profit after tax tells a three-act story. Losses of ₹0.27 crore in FY2013 and ₹0.12 crore in FY2014; then ₹1.50 crore in FY2015, ₹0.90 crore in FY2016, ₹1.75 crore in FY2017; then ₹1.33 crore in the six months to September 30, 2017.

Earnings per share runs the same shape, which matters because it is the only per-share earnings anchor the excerpts give: (₹0.45) in FY2013, (₹0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017 and ₹1.48 in the first half of FY2018.

Operating cash flow is the number that does not fit the pattern. It was positive for four straight years — ₹2.01 crore in FY2013, ₹1.28 crore in FY2014, ₹4.22 crore in FY2015 and ₹8.03 crore in FY2016 — then swung to an outflow of ₹3.50 crore in FY2017, recovering to an inflow of ₹1.25 crore in the six months to September 30, 2017.

Total assets moved the other way for a while and then grew: ₹30.19 crore at March 2013, ₹26.79 crore at March 2014, ₹25.93 crore at March 2015, ₹27.67 crore at March 2016, ₹32.74 crore at March 2017 and ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017.

Off the balance sheet, contingent liabilities and commitments (to the extent not provided for) aggregated ₹29.11 lakh as at September 30, 2017 — small in absolute terms, but the filing lists it as a risk to financial condition if it materialises.

The capital structure at September 30, 2017: authorised share capital of ₹20.00 crore across 20,00,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, and issued, subscribed and paid-up capital of ₹8.97 crore across 89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each.
Three lines the excerpts do not carry: revenue or total income for any period, EBITDA, and the debt level. The report says so plainly rather than deriving them from other lines.

beats.beat: The promoters are Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh and Rajesh C. Parikh, alongside the corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited.
Together the promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of pre-issue paid-up equity share capital; the promoter group excluding the promoters holds 21,510 equity shares, or 0.24%.

A 99.76% promoter holding means the pre-issue free float is close to nil. The issue is the mechanism by which any outside shareholding comes into existence, which is why the fresh-issue versus offer-for-sale split would matter — and is not disclosed in the excerpts.

Related-party transactions exist in each of the last five financial years and in the six months ended September 30, 2017, disclosed under Accounting Standard 18 in the financial statements; the filing separately warns such transactions may continue and could affect financial condition and results of operations.

Compliance flags stated in the filing: past non-filings, incorrect filings or delays in filing statutory forms with the RoC; certain statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals not yet obtained for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; the corporate logo not yet registered; and premises at the Plot 347 Waghodia plant, the Thenkasi Road plant in Tamil Nadu and the Bhuj and Udaipur administrative offices not owned by the company.
The company, its promoters, its group company and its directors are parties to legal proceedings, which the filing lists as an internal risk factor.

On borrowings, the filing says loan agreements carry several restrictive covenants and certain unconditional rights in favour of lenders, and that unsecured loans taken by the company, the promoters, group companies or associates can be recalled at any time.
The excerpts do not disclose promoter shareholding after the issue, or any auditor qualification.

beats.beat: Start with scale. The Indian chemicals industry excluding pharmaceuticals and fertilisers was ₹5,800–6,200 billion in fiscal 2017, and specialty chemicals (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuffs) were about 17% of that, roughly ₹1,000 billion.
The specialty chemicals segment grew 10–12% a year from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and CRISIL Research forecasts 12–14%; the same page also carries a ₹1,443 billion sizing figure for the segment.

Growth inside the sector is uneven, and the filing lists it sub-segment by sub-segment: construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients at 15% CAGR, surfactants at 13%, textile chemicals and flavours and fragrances at 12%, polymer additives at 10%.

The demand argument is a consumption argument. GDP grew 7.1% in fiscal 2017, private consumption is 58% of GDP, the urban share of the population was about 31% in 2011 and should reach 36% by 2020, and the Indian middle class could grow to 148 million households by 2030.

Two external supports are named: policy (a Draft National Chemical Policy, industrial licensing dropped for most chemicals, FDI permitted up to 100%) and China's retreat from low-volume specialty work after stricter environmental rules from 2015.
Competition is described as fragmented — SMEs hold 70–75% of the market — with only a few Indian players able to match global giants on product development and innovation.

The filing's own headwinds: chemicals imports have grown faster than exports (6.4% versus 6% CAGR from 2012-13 to 2016-17), EU-bound exports face the REACH regime, GST took effect on July 1, 2017, and competitive pricing pressure is flagged as a risk to revenues and margins.

The downstream industries the filing reviews — paints at ₹401 billion in fiscal 2017, cosmetics and toiletries at ₹430–460 billion, polymer demand at 9–10% CAGR and plastic products at 11–13% CAGR to fiscal 2020 — are the demand backdrop, not disclosed segments of this company's own revenue.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals — functional additives and chemically modified minerals — and also processes and sells soft minerals and hard minerals. That is the whole business in one line.

It is almost entirely a family-and-parent company: the promoters hold 89,48,270 shares, or 99.76% of pre-issue paid-up equity, and the wider promoter group holds another 0.24%. The public issue is how outsiders get a stake at all.

The filing carries six reporting periods — the years ended March 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017, plus the six months ended September 30, 2017 — long enough to show two loss years, three profitable years, and a cash-flow reversal in the most recent full year.
The objects of the issue name a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, general corporate purposes, and a listing on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE).
The excerpts do not give the issue size, the price band, or how much of the offer is fresh issue versus offer for sale. This report names that absence rather than filling it.

intro.purpose: Orient a newcomer in a few sentences: what the company makes, who owns it, how long a record the filing shows, and what the money is for.

beats.beat: A public issue has two halves. A fresh issue is new shares the company sells, and the company keeps the money. An offer for sale is existing shares sold by current owners, where the company gets nothing. Which half dominates decides whether the listing funds the business or cashes out the founders.

The objects of the issue name three things: capital expenditure for setting up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; general corporate purposes; and creating a public trading market by listing on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to enhance visibility and brand.
Vivro Financial Services Private Limited is named as the lead manager to the issue.
Link Intime India Private Limited is named as the registrar to the issue.

The excerpts do not disclose the issue size, the price band, the split between fresh issue and offer for sale, or the identity of any selling shareholder. This report states that as not disclosed; it does not estimate any of it.

offer.heading: The offer: what is being raised, and for what
offer.purpose: Define fresh issue versus offer for sale in one breath, name the intermediaries the excerpts do name, list the stated objects, and state plainly what the excerpts do not disclose about the offer's size and structure.

beats.beat: The company has no long-term or definitive agreements with its customers and relies on purchase orders for volume, pricing and other terms — and no long-term agreements with its raw material suppliers either. Both sides of the trade are exposed to renegotiation at every order.

Sales run through the corporate promoter. The marketing and selling arrangement with 20 Microns Limited is the company's route to market, and the filing lists that promoter's support among its strengths — which makes the arrangement a single point of failure, not just an advantage.

Licensing is incomplete. Statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat have not yet been obtained, and the filing cannot assure the company will not be penalised for that non-compliance; separately, there have been past non-filings, incorrect filings or delays in filing statutory forms with the RoC.
Operating cash flow turned negative in FY2017 — an outflow of ₹3.50 crore after four years of inflows — and the filing states that sustained negative cash flow could impact growth and business.

Legal proceedings involve the company, its promoters, its group company and its directors; an adverse decision, the filing says, may have a material adverse effect on business, results of operations and financial condition.

beats.beat: Valuation usually starts from the outside: take the earnings multiple that listed companies in the same business trade at, apply it to the issuer's earnings, and see where the answer lands relative to the asking price.
The excerpts contain no peer comparison table — no named peers, and no peer price-to-earnings, earnings per share, net asset value or return on net worth figures.
The only per-share earnings anchor the excerpts supply is the company's own restated EPS: ₹1.48 for the six months to September 30, 2017, ₹2.43 for FY2017, ₹1.46 for FY2016 and ₹2.47 for FY2015.
The share count anchor is 89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, issued, subscribed and paid up as at September 30, 2017.
With no price band and no issue size in the excerpts, any implied price range would be invented. It is not provided here.
